title: Semantic versions
description:
npm decides which package versions to install from ranges like `^4.1.0`. Write the core of that logic:

```javascript
function parseVersion(text) { }            // "4.1.0" gives [4, 1, 0]; throws an Error "bad version <text>" otherwise
function compareVersions(a, b) { }         // negative, 0 or positive, like a sort compare function
function satisfies(version, range) { }     // whether the version is inside the range
function maxSatisfying(versions, range) { } // the highest version in the list that satisfies the range, or null
```

A version is exactly three whole numbers without leading zeros (`0` itself is fine) separated by dots. Ranges:

| Range | Allows |
|---|---|
| `1.2.3` | exactly 1.2.3 |
| `>=1.2.3` | 1.2.3 or higher |
| `~1.2.3` | at least 1.2.3, below 1.3.0 |
| `^1.2.3` | at least 1.2.3, below 2.0.0 |
| `^0.2.3` | at least 0.2.3, below 0.3.0 |
| `^0.0.3` | exactly 0.0.3 |
| `*` | any version |

Compare numerically: 1.10.0 is higher than 1.9.0. Any other range throws an `Error` `bad range <range>`.
hints: To check a version, `split(".")` it and look at each part: it must be non-empty, every character must be a digit (`c >= "0" && c <= "9"`), and only `"0"` itself may start with `0`. For a range, `startsWith` tells you which operator comes first, and `slice` gives the version after it.
Compare part by part as numbers: comparing the strings `"1.10.0"` and `"1.9.0"` puts them the wrong way round.
Every caret and tilde range is "at least the base version, below an upper bound". Work out the upper bound once and compare against both ends.
